prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell); airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority; platform receives confirmed capacity impacts after duty coordination. Parts: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; never originates airfield safety judgments); Slot Allocation Engine; Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; Common Situation Display, records duty confirmations); Digital Briefing Room; Tower Sequence Manager (never replaces controllers; receives ramp intent via sync); Ramp Movement Board; Departure Metering Service; Arrival Regulation Console; Contingency Operations Console; Weather Ingest Gateway (WIG, Orchard); Flight Data Exchange; Surface Surveillance Adapter (East/West Apron Sensors, supporting evidence only, to Portal and Ramp Control Lead); Airline Interface Adapter; Alert Distribution Hub; Performance Analytics Warehouse; Audit Event Ledger; Identity Access Service; Business Rules Registry (BRR); Time Synchronization Service; Collaborative Decision Log; North/South Runway Meter; Sector Load Monitor; Gate Conflict Detector (alerts Ramp Control Lead of stand/lane overlap); Handling Resource Planner (baggage, catering, cleaning, boarding, towing resources). Actors: Regional Flow Manager (Copperfin); Airline Operations Coordinator (Saffron; required when resequence affects boarding/connections/rotation); Aircraft Operator Representative (accepts revised off-block expectations); Ground Handling Dispatcher; Ramp Control Lead (Quartzline; reconciles sensors, prioritizes towing, sends Stand Tow Request Form, reviews Planner constraints, escalates congestion to Tower Supervisor and Airport Duty Manager); Tower Supervisor (Brindle); Slot Coordinator; Airport Duty Manager; Meteorology Briefing Officer; Data Governance Steward; System Support Engineer; others. Items: FIM, Airport Capacity Plan, TOBT, CTT, Airport Acceptance Rate, Tactical Regulation Proposal, Ground Delay Program status, Storm Cell Snapshot, Runway Inspection Note, Post Operations Report, weather update, duty coordination alert, Stand Tow Request Form. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode (wider pushback/tow spacing); Capacity Reduction State (prevent stand saturation, keep emergency routes); Recovery Phase. Requirements: Orchard shall issue time-stamped weather updates; Ramp Control Lead shall not release pushback until Tower Supervisor confirms integration; Marlinstone shall refresh stand demand forecasts on material off-block change recorded by Ramp Movement Board; maintenance tows behind live movements; stands occupied from servicing start until safety area clear.

Document units:
S221: All material resequencing decisions are recorded in the Collaborative Decision Log with the reason, affected aircraft, coordinating parties, and time of approval.
S222: The Audit Event Ledger retains movement updates from the Ramp Movement Board so that post-event review can compare planned sequencing with actual apron performance.
S223: Slot allocation within the Regional Flow Platform is governed by operational safety, published capacity, equitable access, and traceable collaborative decision making.
S224: The Slot Allocation Engine is introduced in operating documentation with the local alias Blueharbor for controller-facing references during transition training.
S225: The Slot Allocation Engine proposes regulated departure and arrival opportunities by matching demand from the Demand Prediction Service to constraints supplied by the Capacity Assessment Module.
S226: The primary inputs are the Flight Intent Message, the Airport Capacity Plan, the current Airport Acceptance Rate, runway metering limits, and airspace sector loading conditions.
S227: When a Ground Delay Program is active, the engine derives a Calculated Takeoff Time or arrival opportunity that preserves the declared capacity envelope before local preference is applied.
S228: The Regional Flow Manager owns the final operating policy for priority classes and may authorize temporary rule changes during a Capacity Reduction State.
S229: The Slot Coordinator administers the allocation run, reviews exceptions, and confirms that proposed results are ready for publication through the Airport CDM Portal.
S230: Baseline priority is assigned first to safety-critical, emergency, humanitarian, and national obligation flights, subject to validation by the appropriate operational authority.
S231: Scheduled commercial services are then handled according to the published timetable, declared readiness, airport acceptance capacity, and the fairness rules held in the Business Rules Registry.
S232: General aviation, repositioning, training, and discretionary movements are allocated after protected and scheduled demand unless a specific operational justification is approved.
S233: Fairness is measured across operators by delay distribution, proportional access to constrained capacity, and avoidance of systematic disadvantage over the active regulation period.
S234: The engine shall not improve one operator's position by imposing an excessive delay on another operator unless the rule basis is visible and logged.
S235: The Airline Interface Adapter supplies operator preferences, but those preferences are advisory unless they are consistent with the governing priority class and available capacity.
S236: The Target Off Block Time is used to test readiness, and an aircraft that cannot meet readiness criteria may be resequenced behind aircraft that can use the opportunity.
